context: This schematic illustrates parallel divide and conquer. It specifies no array values, numerical bucket boundaries, or running times. From top to bottom, it shows “Unsorted data,” six buckets, six processing units, and “Sorted data.”
description: Six downward arrows distribute the unsorted data among six buckets. A vertical dashed line connects each bucket to its processing unit. The six within-bucket sorts are independent and can run simultaneously on different units.

Once each unit finishes sorting its bucket, output arrows converge on the sorted data at the bottom. When buckets represent ordered value ranges, their sorted contents must be collected in range order to produce a globally sorted result.

The figure illustrates how independent subproblems enable parallel speedups on multicore or multiprocessor systems. It gives neither the distribution of data across buckets nor the costs of communication and merging, so six units do not imply a sixfold speedup.

frames.explanation: Divide and conquer splits the sort into disjoint within-bucket sorts that multiple units can perform in parallel. Their results are then combined.
frames.title: Parallel structure of bucket sort

summary: Distribute unsorted data among six buckets, sort them in parallel on six processing units, then collect their results in order to obtain sorted data.
title: Parallel structure of bucket sort
